LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen unusually hard for a normally steady defense company — down about a third from its high — even though nothing about military spending or its business has actually changed, which is why it looks attractive here.

ASML.sentence: ASML dropped around 7% over just two days, which is a sharp move for the only company in the world that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, but nothing about the business has changed.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet stretch — industrial gas demand is steady and they slowly raise prices under long contracts, and oddly the best operator in the business is priced no richer than its weaker rivals right now.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft ticked up and is only modestly off its high — the AI cloud story keeps grinding along without any real drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is flat, but biotech funding is thawing, and since these lab-equipment orders tend to follow that money by a couple of quarters, it's a good early sign.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge, the pipeline toll-road operator, pays a generous dividend and is holding steady — fairly priced right now, not a screaming bargain but not expensive either.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow jumped nearly 8%, and even after that it's still well below its high — big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow-automation and AI tools on long-term contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore held up better than the wider copper-mining pack this week, helped by its trading arm, which makes money whether or not metal prices are rising.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta slipped a bit and its reported prices look softer, but that's just noise from acquisitions and geography — the real price it gets for a ton of crushed stone is still climbing nicely.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA, the big Latin American Coke bottler, is quiet — a strong Mexican peso is helping their earnings for now, though the peso is about as strong as it usually gets.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is barely moved, and with oil prices well above what it costs them to pump it, their hefty dividend is comfortably covered right now.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping and logistics giant, drifted down a bit and is now priced below what its ships alone would cost to replace — cheap by that measure while global trade stays subdued.

MA.sentence: Mastercard edged up, and it's now priced no higher than its twin rival Visa despite growing cross-border spending — every tap still earns them a tiny toll, millions of times a day.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot maker rose a bit but is still down almost 38% from its high, even though hospitals keep doing more da Vinci operations — each one meaning more instruments and supplies sold.
